entries.title: Not in an EAI project.
why: The current folder does not contain the project markers created by eai init.
The command needs a project root so it can read local app configuration safely.
You may be one directory above or below the generated app folder.
evidenceToCheck: Current working directory.
Whether package.json and src/eai.config/object-types.ts exist.
Whether eai verify reports the same project-root issue.

diagnostics.purpose: Confirm the current folder before changing anything.
Check whether the current folder is an EAI project.
If this is an EAI project, inspect template drift without writing files.

fixes.purpose: Move into a folder that has already been initialized.
Create a new EAI app project when this folder should become one.

stopWhen: The folder still has no EAI project markers after eai init or changing directory.

neededWhen: A freshly generated project still cannot be detected as an EAI project.

entries.title: Not logged in.
why: The CLI does not have a usable local sign-in token.
The token may have expired or been created for a different local profile.
The command needs a user session before it can resolve tenant access.
evidenceToCheck: eai whoami status.
Active profile, if a local profile is selected.
Whether the command is running on a machine or Codespace that has completed browser sign-in.

diagnostics.purpose: Show the current login and active tenant status.
Confirm tenant memberships after login succeeds.

fixes.purpose: Authenticate with the EAI identity flow.
Use a fixed local callback port for Codespaces or locked-down environments.
fixes.when: Use when the browser callback cannot reach the CLI.

stopWhen: The browser sign-in flow repeatedly fails with the same identity error.

neededWhen: Login succeeds but no expected tenant membership is visible.

entries.title: Access token expired.
why: The saved user session is older than the identity provider allows.
The CLI cannot refresh the session silently in this environment.
The command needs a fresh user token before it can call tenant-scoped APIs.
evidenceToCheck: eai whoami token status.
Whether the active profile changed since the last login.

diagnostics.purpose: Confirm the expired session and active profile.

stopWhen: A fresh login still returns an expired-token result.

neededWhen: A newly completed login immediately reports an expired token.
include: token expiry time without token values

entries.title: Permission denied.
why: The signed-in user can authenticate, but does not have the role required for this action.
The active tenant may not be the tenant where the user has the needed role.
The app or resource may require a tenant-admin or builder-level action.
evidenceToCheck: Active tenant in eai whoami.
Roles returned by eai tenant list --all --format json.
The exact command and request ID, if the server returned one.

diagnostics.purpose: Confirm the signed-in user and active tenant.
List visible tenant memberships and roles.

fixes.purpose: Switch to a tenant where the user has the required role.
Bootstrap direct child tenant admin access when the user is authorized as the parent tenant admin.
fixes.when: Only when the user is already an authorized parent tenant admin.

stopWhen: The user lacks the required tenant role. Retrying will not change authorization.

neededWhen: No visible tenant membership has the role required by the command.

entries.title: Tenant data-plane authorization incomplete.
why: The app registration exists, but the selected tenant has not completed app authorization.
The active tenant may not be the tenant this app was provisioned for.
The authorization retry may need to run again after sign-in wiring is refreshed.
evidenceToCheck: eai whoami active tenant.
eai provision entra --force --debug tenant authorization summary.
Request ID and platform status if debug output includes one.

diagnostics.purpose: Confirm login, active tenant, profile, and public API context.
Confirm the intended tenant is visible to the user.

fixes.purpose: Select the tenant that should own the app.
Refresh sign-in wiring and retry app authorization for the active tenant.
Create or refresh the current user membership after app authorization succeeds.
fixes.when: Run only after provision entra no longer reports incomplete tenant authorization.

stopWhen: The same platform 5xx or authorization status remains after bounded retry.

neededWhen: The platform authorization step continues to fail after bounded retry.

entries.title: Tenant app authorization could not be completed because the platform returned a server error.
why: The CLI tried to authorize the app for the selected tenant, but the platform returned a server-side failure.
This is usually not fixed by changing local files or repeatedly rotating app credentials.
The safest next step is a bounded retry followed by escalation with the request evidence.
evidenceToCheck: HTTP status from eai provision entra --force --debug.
Request ID if present.
Whether the same status repeats after bounded retry.

diagnostics.purpose: Retry once with product-safe diagnostics and request identifiers.
Confirm the active tenant and profile are still correct.

stopWhen: The same 5xx status repeats after bounded retry.

neededWhen: A platform 5xx repeats for the same authorization command.

entries.title: Tenant plan does not allow this builder operation.
why: The tenant is reachable, but the requested builder operation is gated by the tenant plan.
The CLI cannot self-upgrade a tenant plan.
Read-only checks may still work while write/build actions are blocked.
evidenceToCheck: Workflow readiness status and reason code.
Tenant active status from eai whoami.
Which command attempted a builder write.

diagnostics.purpose: Confirm whether builder operations are available for the active tenant.
Confirm the active tenant before asking an admin to change plan state.

stopWhen: The readiness reason is paid_upgrade_required. Retrying does not activate the tenant plan.

neededWhen: A builder operation is required and readiness reports paid_upgrade_required.

entries.title: Object Type validation failed.
why: At least one local Object Type definition does not match the schema rules enforced by the CLI or platform.
Common causes include invalid default values, incomplete storage metadata, or missing required fields.
Publishing cannot continue until the local definitions validate.
evidenceToCheck: Validation details printed by eai types validate.
Object Type name and property path in the error output.
Whether the Object Type is marked published before storage metadata is ready.

diagnostics.purpose: Validate local Object Types without publishing them.
Compare local definitions with published tenant state after validation passes.

fixes.purpose: Publish the corrected definitions after validation passes.
fixes.when: Run only after eai types validate is clean.

stopWhen: The same validation issue is reported. Fix the local Object Type definition before retrying.

neededWhen: The definition appears valid but the CLI still rejects it.

entries.title: Object Type is not published for the active tenant.
why: The resource command is asking for a type that is not available in the active tenant schema.
The local Object Types may not have been published yet.
The active tenant may not be the tenant where the Object Type was published.
evidenceToCheck: Published type list from eai resources schema.
Active tenant from eai whoami.
Local Object Type definitions from eai types validate.

diagnostics.purpose: List published Object Types visible to the active tenant.
Check local definitions before publishing.

fixes.purpose: Publish local Object Types to the active tenant.
Switch to the tenant where the Object Type was published.
fixes.when: Use when the active tenant is wrong.

stopWhen: The type is still absent from eai resources schema after publishing and schema propagation.

neededWhen: types seed reports convergence but resources schema never shows the Object Type.

entries.title: Workflow runtime binding requires operator assistance.
why: The tenant and workflow key are recognized, but an executable runtime binding is not available yet.
Some workflow bindings require an operator-assisted request before chat or workflow execution can run.
The CLI should request the binding only when readiness reports operator_required.
evidenceToCheck: workflow readiness status and reason code.
workflow status for the specific workflow key.
request ID returned by eai workflow request.

diagnostics.purpose: Check tenant, plan, and workflow readiness.
Check whether the workflow has an executable runtime binding.

fixes.purpose: Request operator-assisted runtime binding for this tenant and workflow.
fixes.when: Run only when readiness or status reports operator_required.

stopWhen: A workflow request is already queued or the status remains operator_required.

neededWhen: The workflow request is queued but does not progress.
